name: 米格尔·德·塞万提斯

points.title: 早年教育
points.description: 塞万提斯出生于西班牙阿尔卡拉-德埃纳雷斯的一个贫穷家庭。他的父亲是外科医生，家境拮据。尽管如此，塞万提斯还是接受了良好的教育，在耶稣会学校学习拉丁语、古典文学和人文科学。这段教育为他后来的文学创作奠定了坚实基础。1566年，他前往马德里，在胡安·洛佩斯·德·奥约斯学校继续学习，接触到文艺复兴时期的人文主义思想。这段时期的学习经历塑造了他对文学和艺术的热爱，也培养了他敏锐的观察力和批判性思维。
points.descriptionEn: Cervantes was born in Alcalá de Henares into a poor family. His father was a barber-surgeon, and the family struggled financially. Despite this, Cervantes received a good education, studying Latin, classical literature, and humanities at Jesuit schools. This education laid the foundation for his later literary works. In 1566, he moved to Madrid to continue his studies under Juan López de Hoyos, where he was exposed to Renaissance humanist thought. This period of learning shaped his love for literature and art, and developed his keen observation and critical thinking skills.

points.title: 军旅生涯开始
points.description: 1569年，22岁的塞万提斯前往罗马，成为红衣主教胡利奥·阿夸维瓦的侍从。这段经历使他接触到意大利文艺复兴的艺术和文化。1571年，他加入了西班牙海军，在勒班陀海战中英勇作战，失去了左手，因此被称为'勒班陀的独臂人'。1574年，他重返军旅，前往那不勒斯服役。这段军旅生涯塑造了他的爱国情怀和坚韧品格，也为他后来的创作提供了丰富的素材。他在意大利的所见所闻，特别是人文主义思想，深刻影响了他后来的文学创作。
points.descriptionEn: In 1569, at age 22, Cervantes traveled to Rome and became a chamberlain to Cardinal Giulio Acquaviva. This experience exposed him to Italian Renaissance art and culture. In 1571, he joined the Spanish navy and fought bravely in the Battle of Lepanto, losing his left hand and earning the nickname 'the one-armed man of Lepanto.' In 1574, he returned to military service in Naples. This military career shaped his patriotism and resilience, and provided rich material for his later works. His experiences in Italy, particularly humanist thought, profoundly influenced his subsequent literary creations.

points.title: 海盗囚徒
points.description: 1575年，在从意大利返回西班牙的途中，塞万提斯所乘坐的船只被巴巴里海盗劫持，他被囚禁在阿尔及尔长达五年。在这期间，他多次试图逃跑，组织其他囚犯反抗，表现出非凡的勇气和领导才能。1580年，他的家人和西班牙国王菲利普二世支付了赎金，他才得以获释。这段囚禁经历成为他人生中最艰难的时期，但也锻炼了他的意志力，并为他后来的创作提供了丰富的素材。他在《堂吉诃德》中多次提及这段经历，展现了人性的坚韧与尊严。
points.descriptionEn: In 1575, while returning to Spain from Italy, Cervantes' ship was captured by Barbary pirates, and he was imprisoned in Algiers for five years. During this time, he attempted to escape several times and organized fellow prisoners in resistance, demonstrating extraordinary courage and leadership. In 1580, he was released after his family and King Philip II of Spain paid his ransom. This period of captivity was the most difficult of his life, but it strengthened his willpower and provided rich material for his later works. He frequently referenced this experience in 'Don Quixote,' showcasing human resilience and dignity.

points.title: 文学创作起步
points.description: 获释后，塞万提斯回到西班牙，开始了他的文学创作生涯。他担任过多种工作，包括税收员和军需官，但生活依然贫困。1585年，他发表了田园小说《伽拉泰亚》，虽然获得一定成功，但未能解决经济困境。1597年，因账目问题被短暂监禁。这段时间，他不断尝试各种文学形式，创作了戏剧、诗歌和小说。1605年，他的代表作《堂吉诃德》第一部出版，立即获得巨大成功，使他一举成名。这部作品讽刺了当时流行的骑士小说，同时深刻探讨了理想与现实的关系，成为西班牙文学的巅峰之作。
points.descriptionEn: After his release, Cervantes returned to Spain and began his literary career. He held various jobs, including tax collector and commissary, but remained poor. In 1585, he published his pastoral novel 'La Galatea,' which achieved some success but failed to resolve his financial difficulties. In 1597, he was briefly imprisoned for accounting issues. During this period, he experimented with various literary forms, writing plays, poetry, and novels. In 1605, his masterpiece 'Don Quixote' Part I was published, achieving immediate success and making him famous. This work satirized the popular chivalric romances of the time while deeply exploring the relationship between idealism and reality, becoming the pinnacle of Spanish literature.

points.title: 创作巅峰
points.description: 《堂吉诃德》的成功为塞万提斯带来了声誉，但经济状况依然拮据。1614年，他发表了《堂吉诃德》第二部，回应了伪作《堂吉诃德第二部》的出版。除了《堂吉诃德》，他还创作了《训诫小说集》、《佩尔西莱斯》等作品。晚年，他继续创作，尽管健康不佳，视力衰退，仍坚持写作。1616年4月23日，塞万提斯在马德里逝世，巧合的是，这一天也是莎士比亚的忌日。塞万提斯的去世标志着西班牙黄金时代的结束，他的作品对后世文学产生了深远影响，被翻译成多种语言，成为世界文学的经典。
points.descriptionEn: The success of 'Don Quixote' brought Cervantes fame, but his financial situation remained precarious. In 1614, he published Part II of 'Don Quixote' in response to the publication of a spurious 'Second Part.' Besides 'Don Quixote,' he also wrote 'Exemplary Novels' and 'Persiles and Sigismunda.' In his later years, he continued to write despite poor health and failing eyesight. On April 23, 1616, Cervantes died in Madrid, coincidentally on the same day as Shakespeare. His death marked the end of the Spanish Golden Age. His works had a profound influence on later literature, have been translated into many languages, and have become classics of world literature.

supporter.zh: 塞万提斯被誉为西班牙文学的巨匠，他的《堂吉诃德》开创了现代小说的先河，通过堂吉诃德和桑丘的冒险，深刻探讨了理想与现实、疯狂与理性的永恒主题。他的人文主义思想和对人性的深刻洞察，使他的作品超越了时代限制，成为世界文学的瑰宝。塞万提斯的一生充满坎坷，但他始终保持乐观和坚韧，他的精神激励着后世无数作家和读者。
supporter.en: Cervantes is hailed as a giant of Spanish literature. His 'Don Quixote' pioneered the modern novel, through the adventures of Don Quixote and Sancho Panza, deeply exploring eternal themes of idealism vs. reality, madness vs. reason. His humanist thought and profound insight into human nature transcend time, making his works treasures of world literature. Cervantes' life was filled with hardships, but he maintained optimism and resilience, inspiring countless writers and readers throughout history.

critic.zh: 批评者指出塞万提斯的作品存在结构松散、情节冗长的问题，特别是《堂吉诃德》第二部被认为有重复和拖沓之处。此外，塞万提斯在政治立场上较为保守，对当时的社会变革持谨慎态度。他的作品中也反映了当时西班牙社会的某些偏见，如对犹太人和摩尔人的刻板描绘。尽管如此，这些批评并不能掩盖他在文学史上的伟大地位。
critic.en: Critics point out that Cervantes' works suffer from structural looseness and lengthy plots, with Part II of 'Don Quixote' particularly criticized for repetition and protraction. Additionally, Cervantes held relatively conservative political positions, showing caution toward contemporary social changes. His works also reflect certain biases of Spanish society, such as stereotypical depictions of Jews and Moors. Nevertheless, these criticisms cannot diminish his great status in literary history.

objective.zh: 在历史学和流行文化中，塞万提斯被视为现代小说的奠基人之一，《堂吉诃德》被公认为西方文学史上第一部现代小说。他的作品融合了现实主义、讽刺和人文主义，影响了后世无数作家。在西班牙文化中，塞万提斯被视为民族文学的象征，他的形象出现在货币和纪念碑上。全球范围内，4月23日被定为世界图书与版权日，以纪念塞万提斯和莎士比亚这两位文学巨匠的贡献。
objective.en: In historiography and popular culture, Cervantes is regarded as one of the founders of the modern novel, with 'Don Quixote' recognized as the first modern novel in Western literary history. His works blend realism, satire, and humanism, influencing countless writers throughout history. In Spanish culture, Cervantes is seen as a symbol of national literature, his image appearing on currency and monuments. Globally, April 23 is designated as World Book and Copyright Day to honor the contributions of these two literary giants, Cervantes and Shakespeare.

self.zh: 自由，上帝赋予人类最宝贵的礼物之一，尤其是那些拥有智慧的人。
self.en: Freedom, one of God's most precious gifts to man, especially to those with wisdom.

others.zh: 塞万提斯、莎士比亚和歌德是世界文学的三大柱石，他们各自用自己的语言创造了不朽的文学世界。
others.en: Cervantes, Shakespeare, and Goethe are the three pillars of world literature, each creating an immortal literary world in their own language.

othersBy: 费德里戈·加西亚·洛尔卡
